# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/patch_webdav_lock.py
"""
Adds WebDAV LOCK/UNLOCK support to webdav.js + CORS allowances to server.js.

Root cause of "Word can't open the file, shows blocked": Microsoft Office's
WebDAV client sends a LOCK request before it will open a document for
editing. webdav.js never implemented LOCK/UNLOCK, so Office's LOCK got a
405 and Office reported the file as blocked/unopenable — even though plain
GET/PUT/PROPFIND worked fine (e.g. "Download and open" and the file browser
were unaffected).

Run: python backend/scripts/patch_webdav_lock.py | ssh roy@192.168.0.181 python3
Then: ssh roy@192.168.0.181 "node --check /home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js && node --check /home/roy/casaos-nas/webdav.js && pm2 restart casaos-nas --update-env"
"""
import sys

CODE = r"""
import sys

webdav_path = '/home/roy/casaos-nas/webdav.js'
server_path = '/home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js'

with open(webdav_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    src = f.read()

if 'UNLOCK' in src:
    print('[webdav-lock] webdav.js already patched')
else:
    # 1. import randomUUID
    OLD_IMPORT = "import { createReadStream, createWriteStream, existsSync } from 'fs'"
    if OLD_IMPORT not in src:
        print('[webdav-lock] ERROR: import anchor not found in webdav.js')
        sys.exit(1)
    src = src.replace(OLD_IMPORT, OLD_IMPORT + "\nimport { randomUUID } from 'crypto'", 1)

    # 2. lock store + XML builder, inserted after xml() helper
    OLD_XML_FN = '''function xml(str) {
  return str.replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;')
}'''
    if OLD_XML_FN not in src:
        print('[webdav-lock] ERROR: xml() anchor not found in webdav.js')
        sys.exit(1)
    LOCK_HELPERS = OLD_XML_FN + '''

// In-memory WebDAV locks, keyed by absolute file path. Office's WebDAV client
// (mini-redirector) LOCKs a file before it will open it for editing — a 405/
// missing LOCK support here is why Office reports the file as blocked even
// though PROPFIND/GET/PUT all work fine.
const locks = new Map() // filePath -> { token, expires }
const LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC = 3600

function lockXml(token, timeoutSec, owner) {
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<D:prop xmlns:D="DAV:">
  <D:lockdiscovery>
    <D:activelock>
      <D:locktype><D:write/></D:locktype>
      <D:lockscope><D:exclusive/></D:lockscope>
      <D:depth>0</D:depth>
      ${owner ? `<D:owner>${xml(owner)}</D:owner>` : ''}
      <D:timeout>Second-${timeoutSec}</D:timeout>
      <D:locktoken><D:href>${token}</D:href></D:locktoken>
    </D:activelock>
  </D:lockdiscovery>
</D:prop>`
}'''
    src = src.replace(OLD_XML_FN, LOCK_HELPERS, 1)

    # 3. advertise LOCK/UNLOCK in OPTIONS
    OLD_ALLOW = "res.setHeader('Allow', 'OPTIONS,GET,HEAD,PUT,DELETE,MKCOL,PROPFIND,MOVE,COPY')"
    NEW_ALLOW = "res.setHeader('Allow', 'OPTIONS,GET,HEAD,PUT,DELETE,MKCOL,PROPFIND,MOVE,COPY,LOCK,UNLOCK')"
    if OLD_ALLOW not in src:
        print('[webdav-lock] ERROR: OPTIONS Allow anchor not found in webdav.js')
        sys.exit(1)
    src = src.replace(OLD_ALLOW, NEW_ALLOW, 1)

    # 4. LOCK / UNLOCK handlers, inserted before MOVE / COPY
    ANCHOR = '      // MOVE / COPY'
    if ANCHOR not in src:
        print('[webdav-lock] ERROR: MOVE/COPY anchor not found in webdav.js')
        sys.exit(1)
    LOCK_HANDLERS = '''      // LOCK — required by Microsoft Office's WebDAV client before it will
      // open a file for editing. We don't enforce exclusivity (single-user
      // NAS), we just hand back a valid token so Office proceeds.
      if (method === 'LOCK') {
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        const token = existing && existing.expires > Date.now() ? existing.token : `urn:uuid:${randomUUID()}`
        locks.set(filePath, { token, expires: Date.now() + LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC * 1000 })
        res.setHeader('Lock-Token', `<${token}>`)
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/xml; charset=utf-8')
        return res.status(200).send(lockXml(token, LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC))
      }

      // UNLOCK
      if (method === 'UNLOCK') {
        const lockToken = (req.headers['lock-token'] || '').replace(/[<>]/g, '')
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        if (existing && existing.token === lockToken) locks.delete(filePath)
        return res.status(204).end()
      }

''' + ANCHOR
    src = src.replace(ANCHOR, LOCK_HANDLERS, 1)

    with open(webdav_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(src)
    print('[webdav-lock] webdav.js patched OK — LOCK/UNLOCK added')

with open(server_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    ssrc = f.read()

if "'LOCK','UNLOCK'" in ssrc:
    print('[webdav-lock] server.js CORS already patched')
else:
    OLD_CORS = "methods: ['GET','POST','PUT','DELETE','PATCH','OPTIONS','HEAD','PROPFIND','MKCOL','MOVE','COPY'],\n  allowedHeaders: ['Authorization','Content-Type','Depth','Destination','Overwrite'],"
    NEW_CORS = "methods: ['GET','POST','PUT','DELETE','PATCH','OPTIONS','HEAD','PROPFIND','MKCOL','MOVE','COPY','LOCK','UNLOCK'],\n  allowedHeaders: ['Authorization','Content-Type','Depth','Destination','Overwrite','Lock-Token','Timeout','If'],"
    if OLD_CORS not in ssrc:
        print('[webdav-lock] ERROR: CORS anchor not found in server.js — skipped (webdav.js patch above, if any, still applies)')
        sys.exit(1)
    ssrc = ssrc.replace(OLD_CORS, NEW_CORS, 1)
    with open(server_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(ssrc)
    print('[webdav-lock] server.js CORS patched OK')
"""

screenshot from the user's own machine authenticating against
raspberrypi.tail8767da.ts.net (frontend-py, pm2 process `frontend-py`,
/home/roy/vaultix-nas-frontend/pwd_2FA_check.py + win_auth_login.py).

Root cause: `allow_credentials` built for `generate_authentication_options()`
(the login-time WebAuthn challenge) constructs each `PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor`
with only `id=...` — no `transports` hint. Without a `transports: ["internal"]`
hint on the credential descriptor, Windows can't confirm the credential lives
on the local platform authenticator, so it falls back to the generic chooser
(external transports: usb/nfc/hybrid-via-QR) instead of jumping straight to
Windows Hello's biometric prompt.

The frontend was never the problem — `static/webauthn_native.js`'s
startRegistration() already correctly captures and sends
`cred.response.getTransports()` (confirmed present in the JSON it POSTs to
/api/2fa/webauthn/register/verify). The bug is entirely server-side:
`webauthn_register_verify()` receives that `transports` array but the
`webauthn_creds` table has no column for it and the INSERT silently drops it
on the floor, so `webauthn_auth_options()` has nothing to pass back into
`allow_credentials` at login time.

Fix (three anchors in pwd_2FA_check.py):
1. Import `AuthenticatorTransport` from webauthn.helpers.structs.
2. `webauthn_creds` table gets a `transports TEXT` column, via both the
   CREATE TABLE (new installs) and a guarded `ALTER TABLE` migration wrapped
   in try/except sqlite3.OperationalError (existing installs — SQLite has no
   `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`), mirroring the ALTER+try/except migration
   pattern already used in mail.py for mail_accounts.type.
3. `webauthn_register_verify()` extracts `credential["response"].get("transports", [])`
   (credential is already a dict here — win_auth_login.py's route does
   `body = await request.json()` then passes `body.get("credential")`, no
   JSON-string case reaches this function despite the docstring's "str or
   dict" — handled defensively anyway) and stores it as a JSON string.
   `webauthn_auth_options()` reads it back and passes
   `transports=[AuthenticatorTransport(t) for t in json.loads(c["transports"] or "[]")]`
   on each descriptor. Unknown/None transports (rows from before this fix)
   degrade to `transports=None`, i.e. today's behavior — no crash, just no
   improvement until that specific credential is re-registered.

Known limitation (by design, not fixed here): existing already-bound Windows
Hello credentials registered before this patch have no stored transports and
will keep showing the generic chooser. The user needs to remove and re-add
the device once (Settings -> Security -> Windows Hello -> remove, then
register again) for the fix to take effect for that specific credential; any
brand-new registration after this patch works immediately.

Run:
  python websites/backend/scripts/patch_windows_hello_transports_fix.py | ssh roy@raspberrypi.tail8767da.ts.net python3
  ssh roy@raspberrypi.tail8767da.ts.net "cd /home/roy/vaultix-nas-frontend && /home/roy/nas-py/bin/python3 -m py_compile pwd_2FA_check.py && pm2 restart frontend-py --update-env"
"""

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/patch_ws_upgrade_api_prefix.py
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Fixes the terminal/collab WebSocket connecting from outside via
https://royhomenas.tail8767da.ts.net (2026-07-13).

Root cause (confirmed with a temporary console.error probe on the live box,
see diag output referenced in CLAUDE.md): `tailscale serve --set-path=/api`
strips the /api prefix before forwarding to the backend on 127.0.0.1:3000 --
same behavior already documented for the /security/scan 404 bug. That earlier
fix added an Express-level middleware to restore the prefix, but this box's
raw `server.on('upgrade', ...)` handler (which is how the terminal and collab
WebSockets get routed) bypasses Express entirely -- Node's http.Server emits
'upgrade' directly, never through the Express middleware chain. So a request
for wss://.../api/terminal arrives at the handler as pathname `/terminal`,
fails the exact-match check against '/api/terminal', falls into the `else`
branch, and gets `socket.destroy()`'d -- which tailscale then reports
upstream as a 502, and which browsers report as an abnormal WS close.

Fix: normalize a leading /api off the upgrade pathname before matching, so it
works whether the request arrives prefixed (direct/local, e.g. raspberrypi's
un-path-mounted setup) or stripped (behind royhomenas's path-mounted proxy).

Run: python backend/scripts/patch_ws_upgrade_api_prefix.py | ssh royhomenas python3
Then:
  ssh royhomenas "node --check /home/roy/royhomenas-nas/server.js && pm2 restart royhomenas-nas --update-env"
"""
import sys
try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
except Exception:
    pass

CODE = r'''# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import sys

path = '/home/roy/royhomenas-nas/server.js'
with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    src = f.read()

# Remove the temporary diagnostic probe if still present.
DIAG = "\n  console.error('[DIAG-UPGRADE] raw=' + request.url + ' pathname=' + url.pathname)"
if DIAG in src:
    src = src.replace(DIAG, '')
    print('[ws-upgrade-prefix] removed diagnostic probe')

if 'p = url.pathname.replace(/^\\/api' in src:
    print('[ws-upgrade-prefix] already patched')
else:
    OLD = """server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => {
  const url = new URL(request.url ?? '', `http://${request.headers.host}`)
  if (url.pathname === '/api/terminal') {
    wss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => wss.emit('connection', ws, request))
  } else if (url.pathname === '/api/collab') {
    collabWss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => collabWss.emit('connection', ws, request))
  } else {
    socket.destroy()
  }
})"""
    if src.count(OLD) != 1:
        print('[ws-upgrade-prefix] ERROR: upgrade-handler anchor not found (or not unique) -- count=' + str(src.count(OLD)))
        sys.exit(1)

    NEW = """server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => {
  const url = new URL(request.url ?? '', `http://${request.headers.host}`)
  // Raw http.Server 'upgrade' events bypass Express entirely, so the
  // /api-prefix-restoration middleware (needed behind `tailscale serve
  // --set-path=/api`, which strips the prefix before forwarding) never runs
  // here. Normalize a leading /api ourselves so this matches whether the
  // request arrives prefixed (direct/local) or stripped (behind that proxy).
  const p = url.pathname.replace(/^\\/api(?=\\/|$)/, '')
  if (p === '/terminal') {
    wss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => wss.emit('connection', ws, request))
  } else if (p === '/collab') {
    collabWss.handleUpgrade(request, socket, head, ws => collabWss.emit('connection', ws, request))
  } else {
    socket.destroy()
  }
})"""
    src = src.replace(OLD, NEW)
    print('[ws-upgrade-prefix] patched upgrade handler')

with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(src)
'''

sys.stdout.write(CODE)

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/patch_xhs_dns_bypass_downloader.py
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Makes the media downloader actually able to download Xiaohongshu (小紅書)
video/image posts, including xhslink.com short links (e.g.
http://xhslink.com/o/Amztl8lJ5yf).

ROOT CAUSE (found by live-testing the user's own link on this Pi, not a
guess): xiaohongshu.com / www.xiaohongshu.com resolve, on this Pi's network,
to 140.111.246.32 -- which is NOT Xiaohongshu's server. It's Taiwan's
National Police Agency Criminal Investigation Bureau (內政部警政署刑事警察局)
DNS-blocking that domain under the Fraud Crime Hazard Prevention Act
(詐欺犯罪危害防制條例); the IP serves a "此網域已經遭到封鎖" notice page.
Querying Cloudflare's (1.1.1.1) and Google's (8.8.8.8) DNS-over-HTTPS
resolvers directly confirms the real IP is completely different (a Tencent
EdgeOne edge, currently 43.170.214.10). This means the previously-applied
patch_xhs_ssl_fix.py misdiagnosed the failure as Xiaohongshu's own anti-bot
TLS trick -- the cert error was actually TLS from the *block page's* server,
not Xiaohongshu's. Confirmed: once connecting to the REAL ip (via curl
--resolve, no root needed), TLS validates cleanly with no cert flags at all.
The user was asked (given the government/legal context) whether to proceed
with a DNS bypass and explicitly said yes.

Additionally, yt-dlp's own XiaoHongShuIE only matches
www.xiaohongshu.com/(explore|discovery/item)/<id> (not xhslink.com directly,
it relies on the generic extractor's redirect-then-rematch, which itself
needs working DNS to the real server) and only writes a single thumbnail
image for image-only posts -- it was never built to grab every photo in a
multi-image 圖文 post. The user's actual test link is a 10-image post, so
that gap matters here. Rather than fight yt-dlp's extractor + the DNS issue
at once, this patch adds a small dedicated handler that:
  1. Follows xhslink.com short links via curl -L (xhslink.com itself is NOT
     blocked -- only the xiaohongshu.com domain the link redirects to is).
  2. Resolves the target xiaohongshu.com hostname via DNS-over-HTTPS
     (bypassing the poisoned local resolver entirely, no /etc/hosts edit,
     no root -- this Pi's sudo needs an interactive password, confirmed via
     `sudo -n true`, so a root-requiring fix wasn't an option anyway) and
     rejects any resolved address that is private/internal (reusing the
     existing isPrivateIp() SSRF guard) before using it.
  3. Fetches the note page via `curl --resolve host:443:<real ip>` (the
     non-root equivalent of a /etc/hosts override, scoped to this one
     request) and parses `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` out of the HTML.
  4. If the note has a video stream, downloads the best
     masterUrl/backupUrls candidate (mirroring yt-dlp's own extractor
     traversal of note.video.media.stream); if format=mp3, transcodes with
     ffmpeg afterward like the rest of this file already does elsewhere.
  5. If the note is image-only (imageList present, no video -- the normal
     case for xhslink.com "圖文" shares), downloads EVERY image, not just
     one thumbnail.
  Media files themselves (sns-webpic-qc.xhscdn.com, sns-video-bd.xhscdn.com)
  are NOT DNS-blocked -- confirmed those resolve correctly and download
  fine with plain curl, no --resolve override needed for those.

  All external calls use execFile-style argv arrays (curl/ffmpeg via
  execFileAsync/spawn), never a shell string built from job.url -- same
  precaution as the existing SSRF/RCE fixes already applied to this file
  (patch_ssrf_ytdl_fix.py, patch_rce_command_injection_fixes.py).

Also removes the now-dead `--no-check-certificate` special-case for
xiaohongshu.com/xhslink.com inside the generic yt-dlp branch of
startYtdlJob() -- it can never fire anymore since the new dispatch check
returns before reaching it, and leaving it in place would misleadingly
suggest yt-dlp still handles these URLs.

Run: python backend/scripts/patch_xhs_dns_bypass_downloader.py | ssh vaultix-pi python3
Then: ssh vaultix-pi "node --check /home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js && pm2 restart casaos-nas --update-env"
"""
import sys
try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
except Exception:
    pass

CODE = r'''# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import sys

js_path = '/home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js'
try:
    with open(js_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        src = f.read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print(f'[xhs-dns-bypass] ERROR: {js_path} not found')
    sys.exit(1)

changed = []
skipped = []

# --- 1. insert helper functions + startXiaohongshuDownload, and dispatch to it ---
OLD1 = r"""async function startYtdlJob(job) {
  if (job.url.includes('douyin.com')) return startDouyinShare(job)"""

NEW1 = r"""const XHS_UA = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/125.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'

// 小紅書 (xiaohongshu.com/xhslink.com)：在這台 Pi 的網路環境下，xiaohongshu.com
// 會被本地 DNS 導向 140.111.246.32（內政部警政署刑事警察局依詐欺犯罪危害防制條例
// 設的封鎖頁），不是小紅書自己的反爬蟲——直接查 Cloudflare/Google 的 DNS-over-HTTPS
// 證實真正的 IP 完全不同。改用 curl --resolve 搭配 DoH 取得真實 IP 直連，不需要
// root、不改系統 /etc/hosts（這台 Pi 的 sudo 需要互動密碼，agent 沒有）。
// yt-dlp 內建的 XiaoHongShuIE 也只認得 www.xiaohongshu.com/(explore|discovery/item)/<id>
// 且圖文貼文只會抓一張縮圖，所以這裡自己解析頁面 JSON、抓完整圖片清單，而不是硬套
// yt-dlp。媒體檔本身在 xhscdn.com（跟 xiaohongshu.com 不同網域），沒有被封鎖，
// 一般 curl 直接下載即可，不需要 --resolve。
async function curlOut(args, opts = {}) {
  const { stdout } = await execFileAsync('curl', args, {
    timeout: opts.timeout || 20000,
    maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024 * 30,
  })
  return stdout
}

async function resolveXhsFinalUrl(shortUrl) {
  // -k: we only read %{url_effective} (the Location-header redirect chain),
  // discarding the body (-o /dev/null) -- the final hop lands on the
  // DNS-hijacked block-page IP (see dohResolveA below for the real fix),
  // whose self-signed cert would otherwise make curl exit non-zero before
  // it even prints url_effective.
  const out = await curlOut([
    '-skL', '-o', '/dev/null', '-w', '%{url_effective}',
    '--proto', '=http,https', '--proto-redir', '=http,https',
    '-A', XHS_UA, '--max-time', '15', '--', shortUrl,
  ])
  return out.trim()
}

async function dohResolveA(hostname) {
  for (const base of ['https://1.1.1.1/dns-query', 'https://8.8.8.8/resolve']) {
    try {
      const out = await curlOut([
        '-s', '--max-time', '8', '-H', 'accept: application/dns-json',
        `${base}?name=${encodeURIComponent(hostname)}&type=A`,
      ])
      const data = JSON.parse(out)
      const ip = (data.Answer || []).find(a => a.type === 1 && a.data)?.data
      if (ip && !isPrivateIp(ip)) return ip
    } catch {}
  }
  throw new Error(`DNS 解析失敗（${hostname} 可能被區網封鎖，且備援解析也失敗）`)
}

async function fetchXhsPageHtml(noteUrl, ip) {
  const u = new URL(noteUrl)
  return curlOut([
    '-s', '--max-time', '20', '--resolve', `${u.hostname}:443:${ip}`,
    '-A', XHS_UA,
    '-H', 'Referer: https://www.xiaohongshu.com/',
    '-H', 'Accept-Language: zh-CN,zh;q=0.9',
    '--', noteUrl,
  ])
}

function downloadXhsMedia(mediaUrl, destPath) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const proc = spawn('curl', [
      '-sL', '-A', XHS_UA, '-H', 'Referer: https://www.xiaohongshu.com/',
      '--proto', '=http,https', '--proto-redir', '=http,https',
      '--max-time', '60', '-o', destPath, '--', mediaUrl,
    ])
    let stderr = ''
    proc.stderr.on('data', d => { stderr += d.toString() })
    proc.on('close', code => code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(stderr.slice(-300) || `curl 退出碼 ${code}`)))
    proc.on('error', reject)
  })
}

async function startXiaohongshuDownload(job) {
  job.status = 'running'
  try {
    let noteUrl = job.url
    if (/xhslink\.com/i.test(job.url)) {
      job.output += '解析小紅書短連結...\n'
      noteUrl = await resolveXhsFinalUrl(job.url)
    }

    const u = new URL(noteUrl)
    const noteId = u.pathname.match(/\/(?:explore|discovery\/item)\/([0-9a-f]+)/i)?.[1]
    if (!noteId) throw new Error('無法識別小紅書筆記連結，網址格式不支援')

    job.output += `此網路環境的 DNS 會把 ${u.hostname} 導向封鎖頁，改用可信 DNS 解析真實位址...\n`
    const ip = await dohResolveA(u.hostname)
    job.output += '已取得真實位址，下載筆記內容...\n'

    const html = await fetchXhsPageHtml(noteUrl, ip)
    const m = html.match(/window\.__INITIAL_STATE__\s*=\s*(\{[\s\S]*?\})\s*<\/script>/)
    if (!m) throw new Error('無法解析筆記資料，頁面格式可能已變更或連結需要登入才能檢視')

    let state
    try { state = JSON.parse(m[1].replace(/undefined/g, 'null')) }
    catch { throw new Error('筆記資料 JSON 解析失敗') }

    const note = state?.note?.noteDetailMap?.[noteId]?.note
    if (!note) throw new Error('找不到筆記內容，連結可能已失效、被刪除或需要登入才能檢視')

    job.title = String(note.title || note.desc || noteId).slice(0, 100)
    const safeName = job.title.replace(/[/\\:*?"<>|]/g, '_').trim().slice(0, 60) || noteId

    const streamGroups = note?.video?.media?.stream
    const videoInfos = streamGroups ? Object.values(streamGroups).flat().filter(Boolean) : []

    if (videoInfos.length) {
      job.output += '偵測到影片筆記\n'
      const candidates = videoInfos
        .flatMap(info => [info.masterUrl, ...(info.backupUrls || [])]
          .filter(Boolean)
          .map(url => ({ url, score: info.avgBitrate || info.videoBitrate || 0 })))
        .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
      if (!candidates.length) throw new Error('未取得可用的影片下載連結')

      const filename = `${safeName}.mp4`
      job.filename = filename
      job.output += '開始下載影片...\n'
      await downloadXhsMedia(candidates[0].url, path.join(job.destDir, filename))

      if (job.format === 'mp3') {
        job.output += '轉換為 MP3...\n'
        const mp4Path = path.join(job.destDir, filename)
        const mp3Name = `${safeName}.mp3`
        await execFileAsync('ffmpeg', ['-y', '-i', mp4Path, '-vn', '-acodec', 'libmp3lame',
          '-q:a', job.quality === 'best' ? '0' : '4', path.join(job.destDir, mp3Name)])
        await fs.rm(mp4Path).catch(() => {})
        job.filename = mp3Name
      }
      job.status = 'done'; job.progress = 100
      return
    }

    const images = note.imageList || []
    if (!images.length) throw new Error('筆記沒有可下載的影片或圖片內容')

    job.output += `圖文筆記，共 ${images.length} 張圖片\n`
    let downloaded = 0
    for (let i = 0; i < images.length; i++) {
      const info = images[i]
      const best = info?.infoList?.find(x => x.imageScene === 'WB_DFT')?.url
        || info?.urlDefault || info?.urlPre
      if (!best) { job.output += `第 ${i + 1} 張無法取得連結，跳過\n`; continue }
      const filename = images.length > 1
        ? `${safeName}_${String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0')}.jpg`
        : `${safeName}.jpg`
      job.filename = filename
      job.output += `下載第 ${i + 1}/${images.length} 張\n`
      await downloadXhsMedia(best.replace(/^http:/, 'https:'), path.join(job.destDir, filename))
      downloaded++
      job.progress = Math.round(((i + 1) / images.length) * 100)
    }
    if (!downloaded) throw new Error('所有圖片下載皆失敗')
    job.status = 'done'; job.progress = 100
  } catch (err) {
    job.status = 'error'
    job.error = err.message
    throw err
  }
}

  if (job.url.includes('douyin.com')) return startDouyinShare(job)"""

    print('[xhs-dns-bypass] ERROR: startYtdlJob anchor not found — file may differ from expected shape')
    sys.exit(1)

# --- 2. remove the now-dead --no-check-certificate special-case ---
OLD2 = r"""  const hasCookies = await fs.access(YTDL_COOKIES_FILE).then(() => true).catch(() => false)
  if (hasCookies) args.push('--cookies', YTDL_COOKIES_FILE)

  // Xiaohongshu (小紅書) CDN presents a self-signed cert to non-browser/overseas
  // requests as an anti-scraping measure -- cert check fails before yt-dlp can even
  // resolve the xhslink.com short link. Skip verification for this domain only.
  if (job.url.includes('xiaohongshu.com') || job.url.includes('xhslink.com')) {

    skipped.append('dead --no-check-certificate block (already removed)')

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/patch_ytdl_pycache_race_fix.py
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Fixes gallery-dl (Instagram/Twitter-image/Threads) failing with:
    ValueError - bad marshal data (invalid reference)
(surfaced in the Downloader UI as "Failed" on an instagram.com job, with a
gallery-dl traceback recommending --verbose + reporting to codeberg.org).

Root cause: "bad marshal data (invalid reference)" is CPython's marshal
module choking on a corrupted .pyc bytecode-cache file. start_ytdl_job()
launches a brand-new `gallery-dl` (or `yt-dlp`/`wget`) subprocess per job via
_ytdl_env(), and _run_ytdl_job_thread() runs each job on its own
threading.Thread -- so two downloads queued close together spawn two
independent Python interpreters that can race to compile+write the SAME
__pycache__/*.pyc file under the shared conda site-packages tree at the same
time. CPython's bytecode writer is *usually* atomic (temp file + os.replace),
but concurrent first-compilation races against a nearly-full SD card
(confirmed 90% full, 5.7G free on this Pi) are the textbook way to end up
with a torn/corrupt .pyc that then poisons every subsequent import until the
file is removed or overwritten.

Fix (two parts, both idempotent):
  1. _ytdl_env() now sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in the env handed to
     every gallery-dl/yt-dlp/wget subprocess, so these short-lived,
     frequently-concurrent child interpreters never write .pyc files again --
     eliminates the *write* race at the source. This does NOT affect the
     long-running FastAPI process's own bytecode cache (only the env dict
     built for subprocess.Popen calls), so normal startup performance is
     unaffected.
  2. One-time cleanup: delete any existing __pycache__ dirs under gallery-dl,
     curl_cffi, AND yt_dlp (gallery-dl's `ytdl` downloader plugin does a
     runtime `__import__("yt_dlp")` for video content such as Instagram
     Stories/Reels, so yt_dlp's own bytecode cache is just as reachable as
     gallery_dl's/curl_cffi's) so any currently-corrupt .pyc gets discarded --
     Python transparently recompiles a fresh one on next import, always safe.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION (2026-08-26, same day, after real-world retest): the
original version of this script only cleaned gallery_dl/curl_cffi and missed
yt_dlp/networking/__pycache__/impersonate.cpython-313.pyc -- a *pre-existing*
corrupt cache file dated back to June, unrelated to any write race. Once
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 took effect, subprocesses stopped writing .pyc
entirely, which means a stale corrupt file that step 2 doesn't reach can
NEVER be overwritten/self-healed again -- it becomes a permanent landmine
that reproduces 100% of the time (not intermittently) on every code path
that happens to hit it. This is why "the fix was verified" on 2026-08-26
morning and then the *exact same* Instagram Stories download still failed
with the *exact same* error message that afternoon: the write-race fix was
real and working, but the one-time cleanup's scope was incomplete. Confirmed
by direct reproduction on the Pi (gallery-dl --verbose against the failing
story URL, with the real cookies file) and confirmed fixed by clearing
yt_dlp's pycache and re-running the same command to a clean exit 0 + a real
downloaded .mp4. Lesson: when a "clear stale bytecode cache" fix is scoped to
specific packages, scope it to every package actually reachable from that
code path (including packages imported *by* the packages you're patching),
not just the one named in the original traceback.

Run: python websites/backend/scripts/patch_ytdl_pycache_race_fix.py | ssh roy@100.109.33.81 python3
Then: ssh roy@100.109.33.81 "python3 -m py_compile /home/roy/casaos-nas/server.py && sudo systemctl restart casaos-nas"
"""
import sys
try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
except Exception:
    pass

CODE = r'''# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import sys, shutil, glob

py_path = '/home/roy/casaos-nas/server.py'
try:
    with open(py_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        src = f.read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print(f'[ytdl-pycache-race-fix] ERROR: {py_path} not found')
    sys.exit(1)

OLD = """def _ytdl_env() -> dict:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env['PATH'] = f"{env.get('PATH', '')}:{YTDL_PATH_EXT}"
    return env"""

NEW = """def _ytdl_env() -> dict:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env['PATH'] = f"{env.get('PATH', '')}:{YTDL_PATH_EXT}"
    # 避免多個下載工作(各自獨立 subprocess/Python 直譯器)同時搶著編譯、寫入
    # 同一份 conda site-packages 的 .pyc 快取檔造成 race -> 損毀成
    # "bad marshal data (invalid reference)"，讓子行程一律不寫 bytecode 快取。
    env['PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE'] = '1'
    return env"""

if NEW in src:
    print('[ytdl-pycache-race-fix] server.py: already patched')
elif OLD in src:
    src = src.replace(OLD, NEW, 1)
    with open(py_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(src)
    print('[ytdl-pycache-race-fix] server.py: patched -- _ytdl_env() now sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1')
else:
    print('[ytdl-pycache-race-fix] ERROR: _ytdl_env anchor not found -- file may differ from expected shape')
    sys.exit(1)

removed = 0
for base in (
    '/home/roy/miniconda3/lib/python3.13/site-packages/gallery_dl',
    '/home/roy/miniconda3/lib/python3.13/site-packages/curl_cffi',
    '/home/roy/miniconda3/lib/python3.13/site-packages/yt_dlp',
):
    for d in glob.glob(base + '/**/__pycache__', recursive=True):
        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
        removed += 1
print(f'[ytdl-pycache-race-fix] cleared {removed} __pycache__ dir(s) (will be regenerated by the main process on next import; subprocesses no longer write any)')
'''

sys.stdout.write(CODE)

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/patch_ytdl_ratelimit_split.py
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Fixes 2 related issues found while investigating a user report of
/api/ytdl/start returning 429 ("請求過於頻繁，請稍後再試") on completely
normal use (queueing 2 links in the Downloader):

1. heavyJobLimiter (10 requests / 5 min) is shared across THREE unrelated
   endpoints: /api/speech/recognize, /api/ytdl/start, /api/ocr. Queueing a
   downloader batch is the normal way to use that feature (paste several
   links at once), unlike OCR/speech which are one-shot actions -- sharing
   the same 10-request budget meant a handful of queued links (plus any
   earlier OCR/speech calls in the same 5-minute window) could exhaust it
   and 429 legitimate downloads. Fix: give /api/ytdl/start its own limiter
   (ytdlLimiter, 30 req / 5 min) and leave heavyJobLimiter (10 req / 5 min)
   protecting speech-recognition and OCR as before.

2. heavyJobLimiter's keyGenerator passes the raw XFF/req.ip string straight
   through without ipKeyGenerator() -- express-rate-limit v8 requires that
   wrapper for IPv6 keys and otherwise throws ERR_ERL_KEY_GEN_IPV6 on every
   request (logged as a pm2 warning each restart, noted but left unfixed in
   the 2026-07-10 postmortem). vaultixResolveLimiter already does this
   correctly; heavyJobLimiter (and the new ytdlLimiter) now share the same
   fixed keyGenerator.

Run: python backend/scripts/patch_ytdl_ratelimit_split.py | ssh vaultix-pi python3
Then: ssh vaultix-pi "node --check /home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js && pm2 restart casaos-nas --update-env"
"""
import sys
try:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
except Exception:
    pass

CODE = r'''# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import sys

js_path = '/home/roy/casaos-nas/server.js'
try:
    with open(js_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        src = f.read()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print(f'[ytdl-ratelimit-split] ERROR: {js_path} not found')
    sys.exit(1)

changed = []
skipped = []

# --- 1. import: ensure ipKeyGenerator is imported alongside rateLimit ---
OLD1 = r"""import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit'"""
NEW1 = r"""import rateLimit, { ipKeyGenerator } from 'express-rate-limit'"""
if NEW1 in src or 'ipKeyGenerator' in src:
    skipped.append('import (ipKeyGenerator already imported)')
elif OLD1 in src:
    src = src.replace(OLD1, NEW1, 1)
    changed.append('import ipKeyGenerator')
else:
    print('[ytdl-ratelimit-split] ERROR: express-rate-limit import anchor not found — file may differ from expected shape')
    sys.exit(1)

# --- 2. heavyJobLimiter: fix keyGenerator + add sibling ytdlLimiter ---
OLD2 = r"""const heavyJobLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 5 * 60 * 1000,
  limit: 10,
  standardHeaders: true,
  legacyHeaders: false,
  keyGenerator: req => {
    const xff = req.headers['x-forwarded-for']
    return (xff ? String(xff).split(',')[0].trim() : '') || req.ip || 'unknown'
  },
  message: { error: '請求過於頻繁，請稍後再試' },
})"""
NEW2 = r"""function heavyJobLimiterKey(req) {
  const xff = req.headers['x-forwarded-for']
  const ip = (xff ? String(xff).split(',')[0].trim() : '') || req.ip || 'unknown'
  return ipKeyGenerator(ip)
}
const heavyJobLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 5 * 60 * 1000,
  limit: 10,
  standardHeaders: true,
  legacyHeaders: false,
  keyGenerator: heavyJobLimiterKey,
  message: { error: '請求過於頻繁，請稍後再試' },
})
// The media downloader gets its own, more generous bucket: queueing a batch
// of links (the normal way to use it) is many requests in one go, unlike
// OCR/speech-recognition which are one-shot -- sharing heavyJobLimiter's
// budget of 10/5min meant a handful of queued links could 429 legitimate use.
const ytdlLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 5 * 60 * 1000,
  limit: 30,
  standardHeaders: true,
  legacyHeaders: false,
  keyGenerator: heavyJobLimiterKey,
  message: { error: '請求過於頻繁，請稍後再試' },
})"""
if 'const ytdlLimiter = rateLimit' in src:
    skipped.append('heavyJobLimiter/ytdlLimiter (already patched)')
elif OLD2 in src:
    src = src.replace(OLD2, NEW2, 1)
    changed.append('heavyJobLimiter key fix + new ytdlLimiter')
else:
    print('[ytdl-ratelimit-split] ERROR: heavyJobLimiter anchor not found — file may differ from expected shape')
    sys.exit(1)

# --- 3. /api/ytdl/start: use the new ytdlLimiter instead of heavyJobLimiter ---
OLD3 = r"""app.post('/api/ytdl/start', authenticate, heavyJobLimiter, async (req, res) => {"""
NEW3 = r"""app.post('/api/ytdl/start', authenticate, ytdlLimiter, async (req, res) => {"""
if NEW3 in src:
    skipped.append('/api/ytdl/start route (already patched)')
elif OLD3 in src:
    src = src.replace(OLD3, NEW3, 1)
    changed.append('/api/ytdl/start now uses ytdlLimiter')
else:
    print('[ytdl-ratelimit-split] ERROR: /api/ytdl/start anchor not found — file may differ from expected shape')
    sys.exit(1)

with open(js_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(src)

for c in changed:
    print(f'[ytdl-ratelimit-split] server.js: patched — {c}')
for s in skipped:
    print(f'[ytdl-ratelimit-split] server.js: {s}')
'''

sys.stdout.write(CODE)

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/scripts/setup_mailserver.py
"""
One-time installer for Vaultix NAS's self-hosted mail server (Postfix +
Dovecot), stage 3 of the "self-hosted personal mail accounts" feature. This
does NOT connect to any Pi from this machine -- it just prints a bash script
to stdout for you to run yourself, same spirit as every other
scripts/patch_*.py in this folder (which print Python for `| ssh host python3`)
except this one prints bash because it's installing packages and writing
whole config files, not doing a surgical text replace in an existing file.

DUCKDNS REALITY CHECK (confirmed 2026-08-21, this is why there's no OpenDKIM
step below anymore): DuckDNS supports A/AAAA records and exactly ONE TXT
record PER ACCOUNT (not even per-subdomain -- the whole account shares one
slot, max 255 chars), and has no MX record support and no way to add
records at a different name (e.g. _dmarc.<domain>, <selector>._domainkey.
<domain> -- both required for DMARC/DKIM to be checkable) at all. Given
that, this setup only publishes SPF (the one thing that fits in the single
TXT slot and needs no extra DNS name), and mail acceptance for INBOUND mail
relies on receivers falling back to the domain's own A record when no MX
exists (RFC 5321 5.1's implicit-MX fallback) -- most MTAs do this, but it
is non-standard and some strict receivers will simply refuse to try. If you
ever move to a real registered domain with a full-featured DNS host (e.g.
Cloudflare), OpenDKIM can be added back; ask before re-adding it here.

PREREQUISITES (must already be true before running this):
  - You've registered a DuckDNS subdomain (e.g. vaultix.duckdns.org) at
    duckdns.org yourself (this script never touches your DuckDNS account).
  - You've put DUCKDNS_TOKEN=<your token> and DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN=<e.g. vaultix>
    in this Pi's /home/roy/casaos-nas/.env yourself (this script reads them,
    never writes .env -- same rule as every other secret in this project).
  - Port 25/tcp (and ideally 587/tcp) is forwarded from your router to this
    Pi's LAN IP. Nothing in this script can do that for you.
  - You understand and accept: a residential IP has no PTR record and very
    likely no sending reputation, and DuckDNS cannot publish MX/DKIM/DMARC,
    so Gmail/Yahoo may still reject or spam-box mail sent from here (or
    refuse to deliver mail TO here) even after this script runs
    successfully. This script maximizes what SPF/STARTTLS can do under
    DuckDNS's limits; it cannot fix IP reputation, get you a PTR record, or
    manufacture DNS record types DuckDNS doesn't support.

USAGE:
  python websites/backend/scripts/setup_mailserver.py <your-domain> | ssh vaultix-pi bash

  Example:
  python websites/backend/scripts/setup_mailserver.py vaultix.duckdns.org | ssh vaultix-pi bash

WHAT IT DOES (idempotent -- safe to re-run):
  1. Installs postfix, dovecot-imapd, dovecot-lmtpd (pre-seeds debconf so the
     postfix install doesn't hang on an interactive "mail configuration
     type" dialog).
  2. Configures Postfix as a virtual-mailbox-domain MTA: recipients/passwords
     are looked up in the SAME MariaDB the rest of the NAS already uses (via
     the `local_mailboxes` table, see websites/backend/data/local_mailboxes.sql),
     reading DB credentials out of the NAS's own /home/roy/casaos-nas/.env
     rather than needing root/new credentials (same lesson as the project's
     other DB-reading scripts: use the app's own .env creds, not root).
  3. Configures Dovecot: IMAP bound to 127.0.0.1 ONLY (mail.py's local-mailbox
     accounts connect here, never exposed to the internet), LMTP for Postfix
     final delivery, SQL passdb/userdb pointed at the same table.
  4. Installs a systemd timer that curls DuckDNS's update URL every 5
     minutes (using DUCKDNS_TOKEN/DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN from .env) so the A
     record keeps following this Pi's public IP even though it's dynamic --
     mail delivery breaks silently if this drifts, since there's no MX
     record for a strict receiver to double-check against.
  5. Adds a scoped /etc/sudoers.d/casaos-mail NOPASSWD entry (ufw, and
     systemctl status/reload/restart for postfix/dovecot only) so
     the new /api/mail/server/* endpoints in server.py (see
     patch_mailserver_endpoints.py) can check/reload these services without
     a password -- validated with `visudo -c` on a temp file before install,
     so a typo can't lock out sudo.
  6. Opens UFW 25/tcp and 587/tcp.

At the end it prints the one DNS record to publish on DuckDNS (SPF TXT) plus
the implicit-MX/no-DKIM/no-DMARC caveats -- then use the "Mail Server Setup"
admin panel in the NAS UI to verify and provision your own mailbox.
"""
import sys

try:
    # Windows' text-mode stdout translates embedded "\n" to "\r\n" on write
    # (os.linesep) by default -- this script prints a BASH script (not
    # Python, unlike every other scripts/patch_*.py in this folder), and
    # bash chokes on the injected \r ($'\r': command not found, mangled
    # heredoc terminators). Force LF-only output so `| ssh host bash` gets
    # byte-identical line endings to what's in this source file.
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
except Exception:
    pass

if len(sys.argv) != 2 or not sys.argv[1].strip():
    sys.stderr.write("Usage: python setup_mailserver.py <your-duckdns-domain> | ssh vaultix-pi bash\n")
    sys.exit(1)

DOMAIN = sys.argv[1].strip()
if not all(c.isalnum() or c in ".-" for c in DOMAIN):
    sys.stderr.write("Domain must be plain ASCII letters/digits/dots/hyphens only.\n")
    sys.exit(1)

CODE = r"""#!/bin/bash
set -e
DOMAIN="__DOMAIN__"
CASAOS_DIR="/home/roy/casaos-nas"
ENV_FILE="$CASAOS_DIR/.env"
MARKER="/etc/vaultix-mailserver-installed"

echo "== Vaultix mail server setup for domain: $DOMAIN =="

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: $ENV_FILE not found -- run this on the Pi where casaos-nas is deployed." >&2
  exit 1
fi

DB_HOST=$(grep -E '^DB_HOST=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)
DB_USER=$(grep -E '^DB_USER=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)
DB_PASSWORD=$(grep -E '^DB_PASSWORD=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)
DB_NAME=$(grep -E '^DB_NAME=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)
DB_HOST="${DB_HOST:-localhost}"
DB_NAME="${DB_NAME:-casaos_nas}"
DUCKDNS_TOKEN=$(grep -E '^DUCKDNS_TOKEN=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)
DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN=$(grep -E '^DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN=' "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2-)

if [ -z "$DB_USER" ] || [ -z "$DB_PASSWORD" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: could not read DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD from $ENV_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$DUCKDNS_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: could not read DUCKDNS_TOKEN/DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN from $ENV_FILE -- add both yourself (from duckdns.org's dashboard) before running this." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "== Step 1: packages =="
if [ -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  echo "already installed once (see $MARKER), skipping apt-get install (config below still re-applies)"
else
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  echo "postfix postfix/main_mailer_type select Internet Site" | sudo debconf-set-selections
  echo "postfix postfix/mailname string $DOMAIN" | sudo debconf-set-selections
  sudo apt-get update -y
  # dovecot-mysql is required for the `mysql { ... }` / `passdb sql { ... }`
  # blocks in Step 3 below -- without it doveconf fails with "Unknown
  # section name: mysql" because the MySQL driver plugin is a separate
  # package from dovecot-core on Debian, not bundled in.
  sudo apt-get install -y postfix dovecot-imapd dovecot-lmtpd dovecot-mysql
fi

echo "== Step 2: Postfix virtual-mailbox-domain config (MariaDB-backed) =="
sudo mkdir -p /etc/postfix/sql

cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/postfix/sql/mysql-virtual-mailbox-domains.cf > /dev/null
user = $DB_USER
password = $DB_PASSWORD
hosts = $DB_HOST
dbname = $DB_NAME
query = SELECT 1 FROM local_mailboxes WHERE domain='%s' AND enabled=1 LIMIT 1
EOF

cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/postfix/sql/mysql-virtual-mailbox-maps.cf > /dev/null
user = $DB_USER
password = $DB_PASSWORD
hosts = $DB_HOST
dbname = $DB_NAME
query = SELECT CONCAT(domain,'/',local_part,'/') FROM local_mailboxes WHERE local_part='%u' AND domain='%d' AND enabled=1
EOF

sudo chmod 640 /etc/postfix/sql/*.cf
sudo chgrp postfix /etc/postfix/sql/*.cf

sudo postconf -e "myhostname = $DOMAIN"
sudo postconf -e "mydestination = localhost"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_mailbox_domains = mysql:/etc/postfix/sql/mysql-virtual-mailbox-domains.cf"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_mailbox_maps = mysql:/etc/postfix/sql/mysql-virtual-mailbox-maps.cf"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_mailbox_base = /var/mail/vhosts"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_minimum_uid = 100"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_uid_maps = static:5000"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_gid_maps = static:5000"
sudo postconf -e "virtual_transport = lmtp:unix:private/dovecot-lmtp"
sudo postconf -e "smtpd_sasl_type = dovecot"
sudo postconf -e "smtpd_sasl_path = private/auth"
sudo postconf -e "smtpd_sasl_auth_enable = yes"
sudo postconf -e "smtpd_tls_security_level = may"
sudo postconf -e "smtp_tls_security_level = may"

id vmail >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo groupadd -g 5000 vmail
id vmail >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo useradd -g vmail -u 5000 vmail -d /var/mail/vhosts -m
sudo mkdir -p /var/mail/vhosts
sudo chown -R vmail:vmail /var/mail/vhosts

echo "== Step 3: Dovecot config (IMAP on 127.0.0.1 only, LMTP for Postfix, SQL auth) =="
# Dovecot 2.4 (shipped on Debian trixie) rewrote its config syntax --
# `mail_location = maildir:/path/%d/%n` and `passdb { driver = sql; args =
# <file> }` (2.3-and-earlier) are BOTH rejected outright by doveconf on 2.4
# ("Unknown setting: mail_location" / "Unknown section name: mysql" without
# dovecot-mysql). Confirmed live against this project's actual Pi
# (dovecot-core 1:2.4.1+dfsg1, 2026-08-21) by iterating with `doveconf -n`
# until it loaded clean, then `systemctl restart dovecot`+`postfix`
# succeeded -- this is not guesswork.

# mail_driver/mail_path replace the old single mail_location setting. Cover
# both possible starting states: a fresh dovecot-core install ships these
# ACTIVE (uncommented) as `mail_driver = mbox` / `mail_path = %{home}/mail`,
# so update-in-place if present, else append.
if grep -q '^mail_driver = ' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf; then
  sudo sed -i 's|^mail_driver = .*|mail_driver = maildir|' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf
else
  echo "mail_driver = maildir" | sudo tee -a /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf > /dev/null
fi
if grep -q '^mail_path = ' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf; then
  sudo sed -i 's|^mail_path = .*|mail_path = /var/mail/vhosts/%{domain}/%{user}|' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf
else
  echo 'mail_path = /var/mail/vhosts/%{domain}/%{user}' | sudo tee -a /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf > /dev/null
fi
# Clean up a stray mail_location line if an older/broken run of this script
# (pre this fix) already appended the invalid 2.3-style setting.
sudo sed -i '/^mail_location = /d' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-mail.conf

sudo sed -i "s|^#\?listen =.*|listen = 127.0.0.1|" /etc/dovecot/dovecot.conf 2>/dev/null || \
  echo "listen = 127.0.0.1" | sudo tee -a /etc/dovecot/dovecot.conf > /dev/null

sudo sed -i "s|^!include auth-system.conf.ext|#!include auth-system.conf.ext|" /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-auth.conf 2>/dev/null || true
grep -q '^!include auth-sql.conf.ext' /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-auth.conf || \
  echo "!include auth-sql.conf.ext" | sudo tee -a /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-auth.conf > /dev/null

# dovecot-core ships /etc/dovecot/conf.d/auth-sql.conf.ext by default, fully
# populated with commented example text (NOT absent) -- a `[ ! -f ... ]`
# guard here is always false after the package installs, so it silently
# skips writing our real config every single run. Always overwrite instead;
# content is fully deterministic from .env so this stays idempotent. This
# also replaces the old separate /etc/dovecot/sql/dovecot-sql.conf.ext file
# (2.3-style `driver = sql; args = <file>`) -- 2.4 defines the DB connection
# and passdb/userdb inline via `sql_driver` + a named `mysql { ... }` block,
# confirmed against https://doc.dovecot.org/latest/core/config/auth/databases/sql.html.
cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/dovecot/conf.d/auth-sql.conf.ext > /dev/null
sql_driver = mysql

mysql $DB_HOST {
  user = $DB_USER
  password = $DB_PASSWORD
  dbname = $DB_NAME
}

passdb sql {
  default_password_scheme = SHA512-CRYPT
  query = SELECT local_part AS username, domain, password_hash AS password FROM local_mailboxes WHERE local_part='%{user | username}' AND domain='%{user | domain}' AND enabled=1
}

userdb sql {
  query = SELECT CONCAT('/var/mail/vhosts/', domain, '/', local_part) AS home, 5000 AS uid, 5000 AS gid FROM local_mailboxes WHERE local_part='%{user | username}' AND domain='%{user | domain}' AND enabled=1
  iterate_query = SELECT local_part AS username, domain FROM local_mailboxes WHERE enabled=1
}
EOF
# This file now embeds the DB password in plaintext -- dovecot-core ships it
# world-readable (root:root 0644), which would leak the DB password to any
# local user/process. Lock it down like the old dovecot-sql.conf.ext was.
sudo chmod 640 /etc/dovecot/conf.d/auth-sql.conf.ext
sudo chown root:dovecot /etc/dovecot/conf.d/auth-sql.conf.ext
# Remove the orphaned pre-fix connection file if a prior run created it; it's
# no longer read by anything (replaced by the inline block above).
sudo rm -f /etc/dovecot/sql/dovecot-sql.conf.ext

# Same "package ships this pre-populated with commented examples" trap as
# above -- the stock 10-master.conf already contains a COMMENTED-OUT example
# `#unix_listener /var/spool/postfix/private/auth {` block, so a plain
# `grep -q "unix_listener /var/spool/postfix/private/auth"` (no anchor)
# matches the comment and permanently skips adding the real, uncommented
# block. Use an unambiguous marker instead.
if ! grep -q "vaultix-mail-postfix-sockets" /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-master.conf; then
  cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee -a /etc/dovecot/conf.d/10-master.conf > /dev/null

# vaultix-mail-postfix-sockets
service auth {
  unix_listener /var/spool/postfix/private/auth {
    mode = 0666
    user = postfix
    group = postfix
  }
}
service lmtp {
  unix_listener /var/spool/postfix/private/dovecot-lmtp {
    mode = 0600
    user = postfix
    group = postfix
  }
}
EOF
  echo "10-master.conf: added postfix auth/lmtp sockets"
else
  echo "10-master.conf: already has postfix sockets"
fi

echo "== Step 4: DuckDNS dynamic IP updater (systemd timer, every 5 min) =="
sudo mkdir -p /etc/vaultix-duckdns
cat <<EOF | sudo tee /etc/vaultix-duckdns/update.sh > /dev/null
#!/bin/bash
# Keeps $DOMAIN's A record pointed at this Pi's current public IP. DuckDNS
# has no MX record, so mail delivery relies on receivers falling back to
# THIS A record -- if it drifts, inbound mail silently breaks with no
# warning anywhere else, hence a 5-minute timer rather than a slower one.
curl -fsS "https://www.duckdns.org/update?domains=$DUCKDNS_SUBDOMAIN&token=$DUCKDNS_TOKEN&ip=" -o /var/log/duckdns-update.log
EOF
sudo chmod 700 /etc/vaultix-duckdns/update.sh

cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/vaultix-duckdns.service > /dev/null
[Unit]
Description=Vaultix NAS - DuckDNS dynamic IP updater

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/etc/vaultix-duckdns/update.sh
EOF

cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/vaultix-duckdns.timer > /dev/null
[Unit]
Description=Run vaultix-duckdns.service every 5 minutes

[Timer]
OnBootSec=30
OnUnitActiveSec=5min
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now vaultix-duckdns.timer
sudo systemctl start vaultix-duckdns.service
echo "DuckDNS updater: $(cat /var/log/duckdns-update.log 2>/dev/null || echo '(no output yet)')"

echo "== Step 5: sudoers allowlist for mail-server admin actions (validated before install) =="
TMP_SUDOERS=$(mktemp)
cat <<'EOF' > "$TMP_SUDOERS"
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/ufw
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl status postfix, /bin/systemctl status dovecot, /bin/systemctl status vaultix-duckdns.timer
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl reload postfix, /bin/systemctl reload dovecot
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl restart postfix, /bin/systemctl restart dovecot
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/postqueue
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/mkdir -p /var/mail/vhosts/*
roy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/chown -R vmail\:vmail /var/mail/vhosts/*
EOF
if sudo visudo -c -f "$TMP_SUDOERS"; then
  sudo cp "$TMP_SUDOERS" /etc/sudoers.d/casaos-mail
  sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/casaos-mail
  echo "sudoers: /etc/sudoers.d/casaos-mail installed"
else
  echo "ERROR: generated sudoers file failed visudo -c, NOT installed" >&2
  rm -f "$TMP_SUDOERS"
  exit 1
fi
rm -f "$TMP_SUDOERS"

echo "== Step 6: firewall =="
sudo ufw allow 25/tcp || true
sudo ufw allow 587/tcp || true

echo "== Step 7: start services =="
sudo systemctl restart dovecot
sudo systemctl restart postfix

sudo touch "$MARKER"

echo ""
echo "================================================================"
echo "DONE. Publish this DNS record on DuckDNS for $DOMAIN, then use"
echo "the NAS admin 'Mail Server Setup' panel to verify + provision a"
echo "mailbox for yourself."
echo "================================================================"
echo ""
echo "TXT $DOMAIN  ->  v=spf1 a ~all"
echo "(set it via DuckDNS's own dashboard/update API 'txt=' param --"
echo " this is the ONLY txt record your DuckDNS account can hold across"
echo " ALL your subdomains, so don't add anything else to it later or"
echo " this SPF record will be silently overwritten)"
echo ""
echo "DUCKDNS LIMITS THAT APPLY HERE (confirmed, not guesses):"
echo "  - No MX record support at all. Inbound mail relies on receivers"
echo "    falling back to the A record above (RFC 5321 5.1 implicit MX)."
echo "    Most MTAs do this; some strict ones will simply refuse."
echo "  - Only one TXT record for your whole DuckDNS account -- so no"
echo "    DKIM (needs mail._domainkey.$DOMAIN) and no DMARC (needs"
echo "    _dmarc.$DOMAIN), DuckDNS has no way to create either name."
echo "    OpenDKIM was intentionally NOT installed by this script."
echo "  - PTR (reverse DNS) cannot be set here either -- that is"
echo "    controlled by your ISP, not DNS, and almost no residential ISP"
echo "    allows it."
echo "Combined effect: Gmail/Yahoo/Outlook may still reject or spam-box"
echo "mail sent from here, or refuse to deliver mail addressed to"
echo "$DOMAIN, even with everything above correctly published. This is"
echo "a known, accepted limitation of the free-DuckDNS setup, not a bug"
echo "in this script."
"""

sys.stdout.write(CODE.replace("__DOMAIN__", DOMAIN))

// Vaultix-NAS/websites/backend/webdav.js
import { Router } from 'express'
import path from 'path'
import fs from 'fs/promises'
import { createReadStream, createWriteStream, existsSync } from 'fs'
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'

const MIME = {
  '.html':'text/html','.htm':'text/html','.css':'text/css','.js':'application/javascript',
  '.json':'application/json','.xml':'application/xml','.txt':'text/plain','.md':'text/plain',
  '.pdf':'application/pdf',
  '.png':'image/png','.jpg':'image/jpeg','.jpeg':'image/jpeg','.gif':'image/gif',
  '.svg':'image/svg+xml','.webp':'image/webp','.ico':'image/x-icon',
  '.mp4':'video/mp4','.mov':'video/quicktime','.avi':'video/x-msvideo',
  '.mkv':'video/x-matroska','.webm':'video/webm',
  '.mp3':'audio/mpeg','.wav':'audio/wav','.flac':'audio/flac','.aac':'audio/aac',
  '.zip':'application/zip','.tar':'application/x-tar','.gz':'application/gzip',
  '.rar':'application/x-rar-compressed','.7z':'application/x-7z-compressed',
  '.docx':'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document',
  '.xlsx':'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet',
  '.pptx':'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation',
}

function mime(filename) {
  return MIME[path.extname(filename).toLowerCase()] ?? 'application/octet-stream'
}

function xml(str) {
  return str.replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;')
}

// In-memory WebDAV locks, keyed by absolute file path. Office's WebDAV client
// (mini-redirector) LOCKs a file before it will open it for editing — a 405/
// missing LOCK support here is why Office reports the file as blocked even
// though PROPFIND/GET/PUT all work fine.
const locks = new Map() // filePath -> { token, expires }
const LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC = 3600

function lockXml(token, timeoutSec, owner) {
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<D:prop xmlns:D="DAV:">
  <D:lockdiscovery>
    <D:activelock>
      <D:locktype><D:write/></D:locktype>
      <D:lockscope><D:exclusive/></D:lockscope>
      <D:depth>0</D:depth>
      ${owner ? `<D:owner>${xml(owner)}</D:owner>` : ''}
      <D:timeout>Second-${timeoutSec}</D:timeout>
      <D:locktoken><D:href>${token}</D:href></D:locktoken>
    </D:activelock>
  </D:lockdiscovery>
</D:prop>`
}

function propfindXml(items) {
  const rows = items.map(({ href, isDir, size, mtime, name }) => `
  <D:response>
    <D:href>${xml(href)}</D:href>
    <D:propstat>
      <D:prop>
        <D:displayname>${xml(name)}</D:displayname>
        <D:resourcetype>${isDir ? '<D:collection/>' : ''}</D:resourcetype>
        ${!isDir ? `<D:getcontentlength>${size}</D:getcontentlength>
        <D:getcontenttype>${mime(name)}</D:getcontenttype>` : ''}
        <D:getlastmodified>${new Date(mtime).toUTCString()}</D:getlastmodified>
      </D:prop>
      <D:status>HTTP/1.1 200 OK</D:status>
    </D:propstat>
  </D:response>`).join('')
  return `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>\n<D:multistatus xmlns:D="DAV:">${rows}\n</D:multistatus>`
}

export function createWebDAVRouter(pool, bcrypt, FILES_DIR) {
  const router = Router()

  // Basic Auth against MariaDB
  router.use(async (req, res, next) => {
    const auth = req.headers.authorization
    console.log(`[webdav] ${req.method} ${req.path} auth=${auth ? auth.slice(0, 6) + '...' : 'MISSING'} ua=${req.headers['user-agent'] ?? ''}`)
    if (!auth?.startsWith('Basic ')) {
      res.setHeader('WWW-Authenticate', 'Basic realm="CasaOS NAS"')
      res.setHeader('DAV', '1, 2')
      return res.status(401).end()
    }
    const decoded = Buffer.from(auth.slice(6), 'base64').toString()
    const colon = decoded.indexOf(':')
    const username = decoded.slice(0, colon)
    const password = decoded.slice(colon + 1)
    const [rows] = await pool.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?', [username])
    const user = rows[0]
    if (!user || user.disabled || !(await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password))) {
      console.log(`[webdav] auth FAILED user=${username} exists=${!!user} disabled=${user?.disabled}`)
      res.setHeader('WWW-Authenticate', 'Basic realm="CasaOS NAS"')
      return res.status(401).end()
    }
    console.log(`[webdav] auth OK user=${username}`)
    req.davUser = user
    req.userRoot = path.join(FILES_DIR, user.username)
    await fs.mkdir(req.userRoot, { recursive: true })
    next()
  })

  function resolve(userRoot, urlPath) {
    const rel = decodeURIComponent(urlPath ?? '').replace(/^\/+/, '')
    const full = path.resolve(userRoot, rel)
    if (full !== userRoot && !full.startsWith(userRoot + path.sep)) throw new Error('Invalid path')
    return full
  }

  router.use(async (req, res) => {
    res.setHeader('DAV', '1, 2')
    res.setHeader('MS-Author-Via', 'DAV')
    const method = req.method.toUpperCase()

    try {
      const filePath = resolve(req.userRoot, req.path)
      const prefix = req.baseUrl || '/webdav'
      const hrefBase = prefix + req.path

      // OPTIONS
      if (method === 'OPTIONS') {
        res.setHeader('Allow', 'OPTIONS,GET,HEAD,PUT,DELETE,MKCOL,PROPFIND,MOVE,COPY,LOCK,UNLOCK')
        return res.status(200).end()
      }

      // PROPFIND
      if (method === 'PROPFIND') {
        const depth = req.headers['depth'] ?? '1'
        let stat
        try { stat = await fs.stat(filePath) } catch { return res.status(404).end() }

        const items = []
        const selfHref = stat.isDirectory() ? hrefBase.replace(/\/?$/, '/') : hrefBase
        items.push({ href: selfHref, isDir: stat.isDirectory(), size: stat.size, mtime: stat.mtime, name: path.basename(filePath) || req.davUser.username })

        if (stat.isDirectory() && depth !== '0') {
          const entries = await fs.readdir(filePath, { withFileTypes: true })
          for (const e of entries) {
            const s = await fs.stat(path.join(filePath, e.name)).catch(() => null)
            if (!s) continue
            const childHref = selfHref.replace(/\/?$/, '/') + encodeURIComponent(e.name) + (e.isDirectory() ? '/' : '')
            items.push({ href: childHref, isDir: e.isDirectory(), size: s.size, mtime: s.mtime, name: e.name })
          }
        }

        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/xml; charset=utf-8')
        return res.status(207).send(propfindXml(items))
      }

      // GET / HEAD
      if (method === 'GET' || method === 'HEAD') {
        let stat
        try { stat = await fs.stat(filePath) } catch { return res.status(404).end() }
        if (stat.isDirectory()) return res.status(200).end()
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime(filePath))
        res.setHeader('Content-Length', stat.size)
        res.setHeader('Last-Modified', stat.mtime.toUTCString())
        if (method === 'HEAD') return res.status(200).end()
        return createReadStream(filePath).pipe(res)
      }

      // PUT (stream directly to disk)
      if (method === 'PUT') {
        await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true })
        const writer = createWriteStream(filePath)
        req.pipe(writer)
        return new Promise(resolve => {
          writer.on('finish', () => { res.status(201).end(); resolve() })
          writer.on('error', err => { if (!res.headersSent) res.status(500).send(err.message); resolve() })
        })
      }

      // DELETE
      if (method === 'DELETE') {
        if (!existsSync(filePath)) return res.status(404).end()
        await fs.rm(filePath, { recursive: true, force: true })
        return res.status(204).end()
      }

      // MKCOL
      if (method === 'MKCOL') {
        try { await fs.mkdir(filePath); return res.status(201).end() }
        catch (e) { return res.status(e.code === 'EEXIST' ? 405 : 409).end() }
      }

      // LOCK — required by Microsoft Office's WebDAV client before it will
      // open a file for editing. We don't enforce exclusivity (single-user
      // NAS), we just hand back a valid token so Office proceeds.
      if (method === 'LOCK') {
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        const token = existing && existing.expires > Date.now() ? existing.token : `urn:uuid:${randomUUID()}`
        locks.set(filePath, { token, expires: Date.now() + LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC * 1000 })
        res.setHeader('Lock-Token', `<${token}>`)
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/xml; charset=utf-8')
        return res.status(200).send(lockXml(token, LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC))
      }

      // UNLOCK
      if (method === 'UNLOCK') {
        const lockToken = (req.headers['lock-token'] || '').replace(/[<>]/g, '')
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        if (existing && existing.token === lockToken) locks.delete(filePath)
        return res.status(204).end()
      }

      // MOVE / COPY
      if (method === 'MOVE' || method === 'COPY') {
        const dest = req.headers['destination']
        if (!dest) return res.status(400).end()
        const destUrl = new URL(dest, `http://${req.headers.host}`)
        const destPath = resolve(req.userRoot, destUrl.pathname.replace(new RegExp(`^${prefix}`), ''))
        if (method === 'MOVE') await fs.rename(filePath, destPath)
        else await fs.cp(filePath, destPath, { recursive: true })
        return res.status(201).end()
      }

      res.status(405).end()
    } catch (err) {
      if (!res.headersSent) res.status(500).send(err.message)
    }
  })

  return router
}

// Anonymous WebDAV bridge for a single shared file, keyed by share token
// instead of a NAS account — this is what lets Microsoft Word open a shared
// document directly (ms-word:ofe|u|<url>) without the recipient having a
// login. Auth model:
//   - share has no password  -> no challenge at all, fully anonymous
//   - share has a password   -> Basic auth challenge; any username, password
//                                must match the share's password
// One-time shares are consumed when the editing session ends (WebDAV UNLOCK),
// not on first request, so PROPFIND/GET/LOCK/PUT calls during one open Word
// session all keep working — otherwise the very first capability probe would
// burn the link before the user ever saw the document.
export function createShareWebDAVRouter(pool, bcrypt, FILES_DIR) {
  const router = Router()
  const oneTimeSessions = new Set() // tokens with an in-flight (locked) session

  async function getShare(token) {
    const [rows] = await pool.query(
      'SELECT s.*, u.username FROM shares s JOIN users u ON s.owner_id = u.id WHERE s.token = ?',
      [token]
    )
    return rows[0] ?? null
  }

  function shareValid(s) {
    if (!s) return false
    if (s.one_time && s.used) return false
    if (s.expires_at && new Date(s.expires_at) < new Date()) return false
    return true
  }

  router.use(async (req, res) => {
    const token = req.params.token
    res.setHeader('DAV', '1, 2')
    res.setHeader('MS-Author-Via', 'DAV')
    const method = req.method.toUpperCase()

    if (method === 'OPTIONS') {
      res.setHeader('Allow', 'OPTIONS,GET,HEAD,PUT,PROPFIND,LOCK,UNLOCK')
      return res.status(200).end()
    }

    const s = await getShare(token)
    if (!s || s.is_folder || s.permission !== 'edit') return res.status(404).end()
    if (!shareValid(s)) return res.status(410).end()

    if (s.password) {
      const auth = req.headers.authorization
      if (!auth?.startsWith('Basic ')) {
        res.setHeader('WWW-Authenticate', 'Basic realm="Vaultix Share"')
        return res.status(401).end()
      }
      const decoded = Buffer.from(auth.slice(6), 'base64').toString()
      const pwd = decoded.slice(decoded.indexOf(':') + 1)
      if (!(await bcrypt.compare(pwd, s.password))) {
        res.setHeader('WWW-Authenticate', 'Basic realm="Vaultix Share"')
        return res.status(401).end()
      }
    }

    const filePath = path.resolve(FILES_DIR, s.username, s.file_path)

    try {
      if (method === 'PROPFIND') {
        let stat
        try { stat = await fs.stat(filePath) } catch { return res.status(404).end() }
        const items = [{ href: req.baseUrl, isDir: false, size: stat.size, mtime: stat.mtime, name: path.basename(filePath) }]
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/xml; charset=utf-8')
        return res.status(207).send(propfindXml(items))
      }

      if (method === 'GET' || method === 'HEAD') {
        let stat
        try { stat = await fs.stat(filePath) } catch { return res.status(404).end() }
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime(filePath))
        res.setHeader('Content-Length', stat.size)
        res.setHeader('Last-Modified', stat.mtime.toUTCString())
        if (method === 'HEAD') return res.status(200).end()
        return createReadStream(filePath).pipe(res)
      }

      if (method === 'PUT') {
        await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true })
        const writer = createWriteStream(filePath)
        req.pipe(writer)
        return new Promise(resolve => {
          writer.on('finish', () => { res.status(201).end(); resolve() })
          writer.on('error', err => { if (!res.headersSent) res.status(500).send(err.message); resolve() })
        })
      }

      // LOCK/UNLOCK share the same in-memory `locks` map as the authenticated
      // router above, keyed by absolute file path — if the owner also has the
      // file open via their own NAS login, both paths see a consistent lock.
      if (method === 'LOCK') {
        if (s.one_time) oneTimeSessions.add(token)
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        const lockToken = existing && existing.expires > Date.now() ? existing.token : `urn:uuid:${randomUUID()}`
        locks.set(filePath, { token: lockToken, expires: Date.now() + LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC * 1000 })
        res.setHeader('Lock-Token', `<${lockToken}>`)
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/xml; charset=utf-8')
        return res.status(200).send(lockXml(lockToken, LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC))
      }

      if (method === 'UNLOCK') {
        const lockToken = (req.headers['lock-token'] || '').replace(/[<>]/g, '')
        const existing = locks.get(filePath)
        if (existing && existing.token === lockToken) locks.delete(filePath)
        if (s.one_time && oneTimeSessions.has(token)) {
          oneTimeSessions.delete(token)
          await pool.query('UPDATE shares SET used=1 WHERE token=?', [token])
        }
        return res.status(204).end()
      }

      res.status(405).end()
    } catch (err) {
      if (!res.headersSent) res.status(500).send(err.message)
    }
  })

  return router
}

# Vaultix-NAS/websites/frontend/serve-spa.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Serve the built Vite/React SPA (./dist) with client-side routing fallback.

Mirrors Firebase Hosting's rewrite rule (all paths -> index.html unless a
real static file exists), so deep links like /system work after a hard
refresh. Binds to 127.0.0.1 only — meant to sit behind `tailscale serve`
or another local reverse proxy, not to be exposed directly.

Usage: python3 serve-spa.py [port]   # default port 8080
"""
import sys
from http.server import SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent / "dist"
PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8080


class SPAHandler(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, directory=str(ROOT), **kwargs)

    def do_GET(self):
        requested = self.translate_path(self.path.split("?", 1)[0])
        if not Path(requested).is_file():
            self.path = "/index.html"
        return super().do_GET()

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        pass  # keep stdout quiet; rely on tailscale/systemd logs if needed


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not (ROOT / "index.html").exists():
        sys.exit(f"error: {ROOT}/index.html not found — build the frontend first (npm run build)")
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), SPAHandler).serve_forever()
